questions.title: SI base quantities, power units & light intensity

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Tick only the rows for current and mass. These are the SI base quantities; energy and force are derived quantities.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer:
power = work done / time = (force × distance) / time
force = mass × acceleration, so:
kg × m s⁻² × m ÷ s = kg m² s⁻³

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer:
power = intensity × area
area = 2.2 cm² = 2.2×10⁻⁴ m²
P = 950 × 2.2×10⁻⁴ = 0.21 W

questions.title: Diver — projectile speed, drag force & upthrust in water

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer:
Energy conservation: ½mv² = ½mu² + mgΔh, with Δh = 9.0 − 1.2 = 7.8 m:
v² = 5.9² + 2×9.81×7.8 = 34.8 + 153.0 = 187.8
v = 14 m s⁻¹

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer: As the diver moves downwards his speed decreases (he is decelerating), so the viscous (drag) force, which depends on speed, decreases.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.answer:
resultant force = upthrust + drag − weight
= 740 + 950 − 78×9.81 = 1690 − 765 = 925 N
a = F/m = 925/78 = 12 m s⁻²
direction: vertically upwards (upthrust and drag together exceed the weight)

questions.title: Wire suspending a model planet — stress, strain & elastic energy

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer:
From Fig. 3.2, stress at strain 5.4×10⁻³ is 0.72×10⁹ Pa
force = stress × area = 0.72×10⁹ × π × (1.2×10⁻³/2)²
= 0.72×10⁹ × 1.13×10⁻⁶ = 810 N

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: Draw a straight line through the origin with twice the gradient of wire X (stress = Young modulus × strain, and Y has double the Young modulus). The line should pass through (strain 3.0×10⁻³, stress 0.8 GPa).

questions.title: Alpha decay of nucleus P — decay equation & momentum

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
²¹⁵₈₄P → ²¹¹₈₂Q + ⁴₂α
nucleon number: 215 = 211 + 4; proton number: 84 = 82 + 2

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: The total momentum of a system of bodies is constant (momentum before = momentum after), provided no resultant external force acts on the system (an isolated system).

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer:
By conservation of momentum: m_α v = m_P × 3.2×10⁵ (Q is stationary)
v = (215 × 3.2×10⁵)/4 = 1.7×10⁷ m s⁻¹

questions.title: Transverse wave, infrared region & CRO wavelength

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: A transverse wave is one in which the vibrations/oscillations of the particles are perpendicular to the direction of propagation of energy.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: Infrared (12–28 μm lies between visible light and microwaves, in the ~1 μm–1 mm range).

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer:
From Fig. 5.1, one period occupies 6.0 cm on the screen:
T = 6.0 × 5.0×10⁻¹⁵ = 3.0×10⁻¹⁴ s
λ = cT = 3.0×10⁸ × 3.0×10⁻¹⁴ = 9.0×10⁻⁶ m

questions.title: Double-slit fringes & stationary wave on a string

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer: Any three of: light diffracts at the two slits; the waves from the two slits meet/superpose at the screen; where the phase difference is 0° (in phase) a bright fringe is formed (constructive interference); where the phase difference is 180° (in antiphase) a dark fringe is formed (destructive interference).

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.answer:
Seven bright fringes → six fringe separations, so x = 10.2×10⁻³/6 = 1.7×10⁻³ m
λ = ax/D = (1.2×10⁻³ × 1.7×10⁻³)/3.1
= 6.6×10⁻⁷ m

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.answer: Since x = Dλ/a, the new fringe separation is smaller (directly proportional to wavelength).

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: Draw a cross (×) at the intersection of the string with the mean-position line — this is a node (a point that remains stationary); the fixed ends A and B are also acceptable.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: 0° — P and Q are in the same loop between two adjacent nodes, so they oscillate in phase.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer: 180° — P and R are in adjacent loops on either side of a node, so they oscillate in antiphase.

questions.title: Cell with internal resistance & filament lamp circuit

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Electric potential difference is the energy transferred per unit charge passing through a component.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer:
With S open, only the 6.0 Ω resistor is in the circuit:
V = IR = 0.25 × 6.0 = 1.5 V
Ir = E − V = 1.8 − 1.5 = 0.3 V
r = 0.3/0.25 = 1.2 Ω

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer: The e.m.f. is the same — the e.m.f. of the cell is unchanged when the switch is closed.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer: Any three of: before t₁ the total resistance is constant, so the current is constant. At t₁ the switch closes and the lamp is connected in parallel, decreasing the total resistance, so the current increases. After t₁ the filament lamp heats up, so the resistance of the lamp increases, increasing the total resistance, so the current decreases and eventually becomes constant again once the lamp reaches its working temperature.

questions.title: Neutrino, quark composition of hadron P & β decay

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Leptons — the neutrino belongs to the lepton class of fundamental particles.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: The down antiquark has charge +⅓e, so the other quark must have charge +⅔e to give a total of +1e: up, charm or top quark.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: Meson — a hadron composed of one quark and one antiquark.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer: X is a β⁻ particle (electron) — an antineutrino is emitted together with the β⁻ particle in β⁻ decay.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer: The nucleon numbers of Q and R are equal — β⁻ decay converts a neutron into a proton, leaving the nucleon number unchanged.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.answer: The charge of R is greater than the charge of Q — R has one more proton, so R is more positive by +1e.
